action.message:
Implemented the fix for "Cannot use aggregate over window functions since 4.2" in django/db/models/sql/query.py.

Change: In `Query.get_aggregation()`, the decision of whether to wrap the query in a subquery now also triggers when any existing annotation contains a window (OVER) clause. Added the condition:

    or any(
        annotation.contains_over_clause
        for annotation in self.annotations.values()
    )

This forces window-function annotations (e.g. `Window(Sum("DJR"), order_by=...)`) to be computed in an inner subquery and then aggregated in the outer AggregateQuery, instead of emitting an aggregate directly over a window function in the same SELECT (which PostgreSQL rejects with "aggregate function calls cannot contain window function calls").

Verification: scoped_tests public regression selection ("aggregation") passed — 124 tests, OK.
